title: Oryx Industrial inference integration scratchbook
notes:
Quick brain-dump from 2025-02-14 kickoff w/ Oryx Industrial (Samir/Jade). Mostly for my personal follow-up and to hand off to infra/SEs. -- Context:

- Customer: Oryx Industrial (edge analytics + predictive maintenance).
- Deployment preference: on-prem first, air-gapped factory network; later cloud/Hybrid.
- Hardware: they have an on-prem rack with 2x A100 40GB currently (want guidance for additional capacity). Mentioned potential upgrade path to L40s/80GB next FY.
- Primary use-case: multimodal logs + telemetry -> short summary + anomaly explanation. Typical requests: 6–12k tokens (raw logs) but usually we preprocess to 1.5–3k tokens per call.
- SLOs: 300ms p50 for short summaries (<512 tokens), 1.5s p50 for 2–3k tokens; p99 targets are looser but they care about tail for alerts. Throughput target ~15 concurrent inference streams during peak (sustained), burst to 45 for batch ingestion windows.

Call notes / raw capture:

- Samir: worried about hallucinations when model fabricates root cause for alerts — wants deterministic grounding to sensor telemetry and last-24h logs.
- Jade: security is non-negotiable: "we must keep everything in our VPC and control keys (HSM)." Explicit ask for KMS/HSM integration and audit logs (immutable).
- They have strict data retention rules (30 days raw logs, 1 year aggregated metadata). Need to support redaction pipeline before store.
- Existing infra: Kafka-based ingestion, Flink for stream enrichment, S3 on Ceph cluster for blob store. They want Redwood Private control plane in their VPC and runtime in an air-gapped subnet.
- Want ability to pin model versions and rollback quickly if quality regression observed. Also ask for canary rollout (10% traffic) then 50% then switch.

Technical requirements (captured during call):

- Private deployment: control plane inside customer VPC, runtime nodes inside air-gapped subnet with egress only to internal registries.
- Key management: integrate with customer HSM; RBAC for key usage; ship audit logs to their SIEM (splunk endpoint).
- Model size: prefer quantized-medium models if latency can't meet SLOs. Need guidance on accuracy vs quantization tradeoffs.
- Context handling: support sliding-window + KV cache to avoid re-sending prefixes when doing short iterative prompts. Must monitor KV cache memory growth and provide eviction policies.
- Batching: request batching for throughput windows, but must not violate p50 latency SLOs for alerting flows. Want per-route batching policy (alerts -> no batching; ingestion analytics -> aggressive batching).
- Fallbacks: policy to fallback to smaller model variant or CPU-based path if GPUs saturated. For critical alerts must never drop requests; prefer queueing with priorities.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-request latency traces, and prompt+response hashes for debugging.
- Evals: need prompt-set based quality monitoring daily job. If quality drops > X% we trigger rollback.

Gotchas & risks noted (things to flag):

- Air-gapped install complexity: images/containers need to be volume-mounted from their internal repo. We'll need an offline installer tarball + clear checksum manifest.
- HSM integration: customer expects hardware-backed keys; Redwood agent must be able to call their HSM API (we'll need endpoint and auth flow). Risk: some HSM vendors throttle RPCs -> test.
- Tokenization mismatch: their telemetry contains many non-ASCII chars and long numeric sequences (IDs) -> can blow up token counts unexpectedly. Need tokenization pre-check and truncate strategy.
- KV-cache memory leak potential: if using unbounded KV store for long contexts, memory on node can balloon; propose TTL-based eviction and soft-limits per model-instance.
- Quantization compatibility: some of their in-house fine-tuned models use ops that don't map cleanly to int8 kernels -> plan for fallbacks or quantization-aware retrain.

Initial sizing guess (very rough):

- Typical req size: 2k tokens (after preprocessing).
- Concurrent streams: 15 sustained (peak 45).
- Assume model A ~ open-llm-16b quantized -> ~12 tokens/ms on A100 40GB (wild guess). Need bench to refine.
- Preliminary ask to benchmark: 1 x node w/ A100 40GB should handle 10 concurrent small-summary requests at p50 300ms. For our 15 sustained + headroom, propose 2 runtime GPUs for POC.

Concrete next steps / action items (assignments and rough due dates):

- Evan Park: prepare an offline installer package doc & checklist for air-gapped install + manifest. Due: 2025-02-21. (JIRA RDW-1423)
- Priya Nair: capture HSM vendor API compat matrix and an example integration flow; request test credentials from Oryx. Due: 2025-02-24. (JIRA ORX-56)
- Maya Chen (me): produce baseline perf matrix with 1x A100_40GB runtime for two model variants (16b quantized, 7b fp16). Run synthetic load with typical token distributions and measure p50/p95. Due: 2025-02-25.
- Samir to provide: sample telemetry payload (sanitized) and exact tokenization examples + SIEM endpoint for audit logs. Due: 2025-02-18 (they said will share).
- SE Infra: design per-route batching policy prototype (alerts = immediate, analytics = batch up to 128 with 50ms max delay). Prototype due: 2025-03-03.

Open questions to follow up (for sales / legal / security):

- Legal: are they willing to accept a Redwood-managed control plane that sits in their VPC (we propose a private control plane subscription) or do they insist on fully customer-managed control plane?
- Data residency: we must confirm whether any telemetry can ever leave the on-prem site for backups. If not, we need an entirely self-contained backup/restore plan.
- Billing / metering: they prefer a flat reserved-node pricing vs token-metered billing. Need to sketch pricing for Dedicated-on-prem model.

Notes to self / informal TODOs:

- When running perf tests, log tokenization bytes -> compile histogram of token sizes. Save example edge-case tokens (IDs longer than 256 chars).
- Double-check our KV eviction APIs — add a TTL and max-entries knobs on node side. File an internal ticket if missing.
- Prep a short demo script that shows canary rollback: deploy model-v1 (90%), model-v2 (10%), simulate eval drop and flip back. Need a mock eval harness.

Meeting cadence suggestion:

- Weekly 30m sync for first 6 weeks (tech onboarding), then biweekly for runbook/ramp. Add a calendar invite with agenda: perf bench results, security checklist, installer status.

Relevant snippets to paste into Jira/Confluence when writing the onboarding PRD:

- "Air-gapped runtime: offline installer + manifest, HSM-backed KMS, per-route batching policies, KV cache controls, model pinning and canary rollouts."
- "SLOs: p50 300ms (<512 tokens) for alerting flows; p50 1500ms for 2–3k token analytics; priority queueing for critical requests."

End of scratchbook. Keep this doc as living notes until handoff to delivery.

-- Maya
summary: Working scratchbook capturing kickoff with Oryx Industrial: on-prem private deployment asks, security/HSM, latency SLOs, batching/kv-cache requirements, rough sizing, action items and open legal/billing questions.
